messages:
Ashley: Observed repeated GPU tail-latency spikes in eu-west dedicated pool this morning (03:00-05:00 UTC). p99 jumps from ~18ms to 220ms. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/eu-west-dedicated
Vikram: Looked at NIC counters and proxy traces. Not compute-saturated. NIC tx queue length climbs, then driver drops, then GPU stalls. Pattern: many tiny RPCs from a couple tenants.
Kai: Which tenants? Is it our inference short-request pattern or something else?
Ashley: Top offenders: tenant-B2 (steady small-rtt traffic), tenant-C9 (bursty spikes aligned with customer window). Both are Dedicated customers on the same hot-rack.
Melissa: Product here 00 we need to be careful throttling dedicated tenants. Can we provide an opt-in shaping beta instead of unilateral throttling?
Vikram: Agreed. Proposal: per-tenant egress shaping at the node-proxy layer plus scheduler-aware placement that avoids co-locating high-concurrency tenants on the same NIC. Two parts: 1) realtime shaping (token buckets) 2) placement signal (backpressure label) to the scheduler.
Kai: For immediate mitigation, we can enable soft shaping at proxy: cap short flows to X rps per tenant, allow bursts, and emit a backpressure annotation. That should reduce NIC queueing without killing throughput.
Ashley: Example proxy config snippet (PoC):
```
egress_shaping:
  mode: soft
  default_rps: 500
  burst_rps: 2000
  tenant_overrides:
    tenant-B2: { default_rps: 350, burst_rps: 1500 }
    tenant-C9: { default_rps: 700, burst_rps: 2500 }
  backpressure_event: true
```
Vikram: Scheduler change: if proxy backpressure seen > 10s, label node as "egress_congested" and avoid scheduling new dedicated allocations for tenants flagged high-conn for 5min. Also we should add a placement heuristic: prefer different NICs (if available) or different racks for high-concurrency tenants.
Melissa: Billing/contract question: Dedicated customers expect isolation. If we put them into shaping we need explicit consent or a billing credit. Can we make this a documentation/opt-in beta plus a one-time fee waiver?
Kai: Rollout plan: 1) Hot-rack canary tonight in eu-west (22:30 UTC) with mode: soft, flag-enabled. 2) Monitor metrics for 30 min: node_nic_tx_drops, gpu_p99, tenant_conn_count, backpressure_events. 3) If no regressions, gradually expand to other hot-racks.
ops-bot: Runbook stub created: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/egress-shaping. Incident ticket: #INC-4552.
Ashley: Action owners: Ashley -> push proxy feature-flag and PoC config; Vikram -> implement scheduler label and placement heuristic; Kai -> run canary and watch metrics; Melissa -> draft customer beta invite and pricing note for shaping add-on.
Vikram: Metrics to add to dashboards: tenant_egress_shaping_active, per_node_backpressure_seconds, tenant_conn_p95, nic_queue_len_p99. Also collect small-packet telemetry for 1h retention during canary to correlate.
Kai: +12m into canary: tenant-C9 shows expected backpressure events, nic_queue_len drops 40%, GPU p99 improved to ~28ms. No customer-visible errors so far.
Melissa: I'll prepare a short message to those tenants offering the opt-in and the mitigation timeline.
ops-bot: Canary completed at 5311112240 00 status: success. :white_check_mark:
Ashley: Next steps: open infra epic, schedule cross-team sync with billing/legal for Dedicated contractual language, and put shaping into the Dedicated feature roadmap as opt-in.
Vikram: We should also explore longer-term: per-tenancy NIC QoS via SmartNIC or eBPF at kernel ingress so we don't rely solely on proxy. Filing a research spike for that.
Ashley: Thanks team. I'll post follow-up notes in #eng-releases and attach the canary graphs.
Melissa: Thanks 00 will loop in account managers for affected Dedicated customers.
